observed_behavior: A fresh preliminary reviewer measured all five cold query samples and two of five warm query samples above the 2.0-second ceiling on the fixed 50,000-file workload; the other six full commands, functional parity, and fixture cleanup passed.
expected_behavior: Every one of five cold and five warm query samples must complete at or below 2.0 seconds with identical functional results and no fixture remaining.
impact: Normal Windows host-load variation causes the required portability CI to fail on unchanged product bytes, blocking the approved performance delivery without a correctness, cleanup, security, or privacy failure.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: The symptom is present when any value in durations_seconds.cold_queries or durations_seconds.queries exceeds max_operation_seconds == 2.0.
steps: Build the benchmark-defined repository containing exactly 50,000 tracked files.
Run the fixed five-query fresh-process cold sequence and same-process warm sequence.
Trace each query child process while keeping fixture, stage, query token, revision, and normalized result fixed.
reproduction.sample: Reviewer: five of five cold and two of five warm samples above 2.0 seconds. Controlled local baseline: one query at 1.97–2.05 seconds; split pre at 1.31 seconds, split post warm at 0.45 seconds, and fully split topology at 0.64–0.69 seconds.

root_cause.summary: The combined pre and post git ls-files dirty-inventory commands each trigger an expensive 50,000-path working-tree scan, consuming about 1.6 seconds of a roughly 2.0-second query. Controlled substitution of staged inventory, git diff-files, and untracked discovery removes the tail while preserving normalized results; direct index-path resolution and staged attribute-path reuse keep the complete query at nine child processes.

hypotheses.statement: The working-tree scans forced by combined git ls-files fingerprint commands cause the two-second query tail.
hypotheses.prediction: Replacing only the pre or post topology lowers its corresponding cold or warm latency, and replacing both keeps results equal below two seconds.
hypotheses.falsifier: Latency does not fall, normalized results change, or search remains the dominant child cost.

hypotheses.statement: git grep --cached is the dominant query bottleneck.
hypotheses.variable: Observed git grep child wall time with fingerprint behavior fixed.
hypotheses.prediction: git grep consumes most of the query and fingerprint substitution has little effect.
hypotheses.falsifier: git grep remains near 0.16 seconds while fingerprint substitution reduces the whole query below one second.

hypotheses.statement: Fixture construction or readiness warm-up is included in each timed query.
hypotheses.prediction: No pair of large fingerprint tails appears inside a query, or removing them leaves the query above two seconds.
hypotheses.falsifier: Two approximately 0.8-second fingerprint calls appear inside the query and the controlled candidate completes in 0.64 seconds.

next_action: The implementation writer must first add regression red coverage for split inventory parity, drift detection, captured attribute-path reuse, and the ten-process ceiling, then apply the single fingerprint-topology change and rerun five cold, five warm, and all required full commands.
